title: Porismata: not wealth, magnificent buildings, or nobility
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): it stands as not a perennial plus stable good. whatever good stands as in nobility stands as fragile; (7) Nor in nobility — full belonging toward toil; (6) Nor stands as it in magnificent plus proud buildings. || he who has ample riches exposes them to so many dangers. acquiring wealth stands as full belonging toward toil; (3) Nor stands as it wealth — ye immoderate zeal belonging toward heaping up riches;
pass_b_english: (3) Nor is it wealth — the immoderate zeal of heaping up riches; acquiring wealth is full of toil; he who has ample riches exposes them to so many dangers.
(6) Nor is it in magnificent and proud buildings. (7) Nor in nobility — full of toil; whatever good is in nobility is fragile; it is not a perennial and stable good.
source_text: 3. Neque est opulentia — immoderatum cumulandarum opum studium; opum acquisitio plena laboris; qui amplas opes tot periculis exponit. 6. Neque est in magnificis & superbis aedificiis. 7. Neque in nobilitate — plena laboris; quod boni in nobilitate est fragile; non perenne & stabile.
